title: Inspect MTB suspension before a ride
summary: Check fork, rear shock and linkage for obvious damage, contamination, leaks and abnormal movement before riding.

steps.title: Start with clean sliding surfaces
steps.instruction: Wipe visible fork stanchions and the rear-shock shaft with a clean cloth so dirt does not hide damage or get dragged into seals.
steps.why: Clean surfaces make inspection easier and reduce abrasive contamination around suspension seals.
steps.warning: Do not spray general-purpose lubricant or cleaner onto suspension seals unless the component manufacturer specifically permits it.
steps.check: Sliding surfaces are clean enough to inspect clearly.

steps.title: Inspect the suspension fork
steps.instruction: Look for scratches, dents, visible oil leakage, damaged seals or loose-looking hardware. Compress the fork gently and note any obviously abnormal binding or noise.
steps.why: Damage to sliding surfaces, seals or structural parts can affect both suspension function and safety.
steps.warning: If you find structural damage, significant leakage or abnormal binding, stop using the bike until the cause is assessed.
steps.check: No obvious unsafe damage or major leakage is visible.

steps.title: Inspect the rear shock
steps.instruction: Check the visible shock body and shaft for damage, contamination or leakage, then gently cycle the rear suspension and listen for abnormal knocking or binding.
steps.why: The shock controls spring and damping behavior and should move smoothly through its normal range.
steps.warning: Do not open or depressurize an air shock as part of a routine visual check.
steps.check: Shock movement appears smooth and no obvious unsafe damage is visible.

steps.title: Check linkage and pivots
steps.instruction: Observe the linkage while gently loading and unloading the suspension. Look and listen for unusual play, knocking, loose hardware or rough movement.
steps.why: Rear-suspension performance depends on pivots and linkage as well as the shock itself.
steps.warning: Do not tighten pivot hardware by guesswork. Use the frame manufacturer’s specified procedure and torque values.
steps.check: No obvious looseness, knocking or damaged linkage parts are detected.
